fixture_contract.created_in: D3.5-A5 (mechanical, outcome-independent extraction from frozen A2 records; not created in A4)
fixture_contract.size_envelope: compact: per-channel ordered object_id lists, bridge candidate records, a global deduplicated rerank-payload registry, and identity fields; no full corpus, no full documents; A5 must verify the committed size before freezing
identity_fields: index identity (panda_knowledge_v1 fingerprint 8172f9a6...; 104973 points; 133077 SQL objects)
case identities (g036, g021, n006, g041, g020, n004)
arm/source trace identity (per-cell arm, execution sequence, treatment flags)
per_case_trace_fields: question text / frozen question identity (query + query_sha256)
retrieval plan identity / relevant frozen plan fields (intent, target/version repositories, resolved_versions, concepts, symbols, concept_scopes, required_source_types, source_budgets)
D2 resolution receipt / exact seed identities (structured_resolution_receipt)
per-channel ordered candidate object_ids with per-channel rank and channel name (exact, dense, sparse, paper when present, workflow, graph)
bridge candidate IDs with provenance origin identities, source_id, source_version_id, locator
unbridged graph ordering (UNBRIDGED cell graph ranking)
bridged graph ordering (BRIDGED cell graph ranking)
frozen fusion weights (exact 2.0, dense 1.0, sparse 1.0, paper 1.15, workflow 1.2, graph 0.8; score weight/(60+rank+1))
baseline fused candidate ordering (full recomputed order, not only top-30)
baseline rerank-pool boundary (top-30 cutoff score and member list)

payload_persistence_strategy.chosen: Option 1 — persist the exact bounded reranker payload
payload_persistence_strategy.rationale: Option 2 (stable identities + tracked content source) is invalid: the normalized corpus is gitignored, so no repository-persistent immutable source exists from which the exact reranker input could be reconstructed; Option 1 makes the fixture fully repository-replayable
payload_fields: text payload exactly as used by the reranker (text[:2000] truncation of the normalized record)
payload_persistence_strategy.coverage: global deduplicated registry covering the union of (baseline fused top-30 members) and (all bridge candidates) per cell; channel-trace members outside this union need IDs only

outcome_label_cleanliness.evaluator_metadata: lives only in a separate evaluator-side file (suggested evaluation/d3_5_downstream_replay_evaluator_metadata.json), never in the runtime treatment fixture

reranker_variance_contract.not_fully_deterministic: a paired replay still invokes the reranker model separately on baseline and treatment pools, so the observed final difference may contain admission/selectivity treatment effect + reranker execution variance unless variance is handled by preregistered symmetric repeated execution

strategy_rationale.R1_chosen: the reranker is a temperature-0 LLM call with an observed execution-variance class (A2 n006 R@5/MRR spread with final evidence arm-stable; D3-A2 n022 e3 precedent); running baseline and treatment pools the same preregistered number of times on the same frozen trace and comparing distributions is the smallest methodology that accounts for it
strategy_rationale.R2_rejected: no deterministic reranker surface exists in the system (the only rerank path is vertex generate_json with RERANK_SYSTEM_PROMPT); inventing one is prohibited
strategy_rationale.R3_rejected: single paired calls leave reranker variance unresolved exactly where the primary admission question is decided; weak inference is not proportionate for the A6 primary question

reranker_variance_contract.repetition_count_rule: a small fixed preregistered repetition count per pool per cell is frozen in the A6 preregistration from a generic stability rationale (bounded, no Monte Carlo sweeps, no heavy significance frameworks); it must not be chosen from A2 outcomes
reranker_variance_contract.over_engineering_boundary: no large reranker sweeps, no arbitrary confidence frameworks, no heavy significance testing

selectivity_problem_definition.governance_eligibility: GOVERNANCE ELIGIBILITY answers: which candidates are governable and therefore eligible to exist (accepted governed provenance, exact source/version qualification) — remains a hard prerequisite
selectivity_problem_definition.query_relevance: QUERY RELEVANCE answers: which governed candidates are most relevant to this query under a tight downstream budget — currently unanswered
selectivity_problem_definition.distinction: GOVERNANCE ELIGIBILITY != QUERY RELEVANCE; selectivity operates only among already governed bridge candidates and never admits ungoverned content

current_cap_behavior.ordering: candidate materialization is primarily governed/provenance-order bounded (insertion order of provenance instances), not a dedicated candidate-level query-relevance ranking
current_cap_behavior.conclusion: candidate cap != selectivity policy; the cap bounds breadth but does not rank by relevance, which is why g021 admitted 19 README-evidence objects alongside prod_sim_hvmaps.C and g020 filled all 20 slots from one fan-out

A_exact_lexical_overlap_with_query_conce.rationale: deterministic, query-grounded, already computed for the normal pipeline (analyzer deterministic parse + frozen plan concepts/symbols); zero model calls

B_sparse_retrieval_score_or_rank.rationale: reusing non-graph channel support as relevance evidence; circularity risk (see below) forbids it as a hard requirement

D_existing_fused_evidence_from_non_graph.rationale: useful relevance signal; must never become extra structured vote + extra sparse/dense vote + forced admission without explicit accounting (no duplicate authority)

E_source_repository_scope_match_from_fro.rationale: deterministic, plan-governed scope; filters only within already governed candidates; no repository widening

F_deterministic_locator_title_token_over.rationale: same deterministic query-grounded family as A (locator paths and titles carry strong file-level signals); zero model calls

G_provenance_distance_structural_path_co.rationale: a shorter governed path may receive a weak deterministic preference, but short path != query relevance; never the sole rule; final tie-break role only

H_provenance_origin_confidence_governanc.rationale: all 16 accepted curated relations in the frozen D1 carry uniform confidence 1.0 and accepted review status — no discriminating signal exists at candidate level

circularity_analysis.failure_mode: a selectivity rule that keeps only bridge candidates already ranked highly by dense/sparse/exact would destroy the bridge's incremental value: in A2 the required files (g036 ana_dpm.C, g021 prod_sim_hvmaps.C) were absent from every non-graph channel when the focused shortcuts were suppressed — that absence is exactly what the bridge exists to repair
circularity_analysis.resolution: non-graph channel presence is never a hard requirement or a removal trigger; absence from dense/sparse/exact must not imply removal; channel support may only add bounded tie-break points in the selectivity ordering among bridge candidates
circularity_analysis.duplicate_authority_guard: channel support influences only the within-bridge selectivity ordering; it never adds votes, never changes fusion weights, and never grants admission by itself

pipeline_shape: generic deterministic candidate relevance scoring (primary: query-grounded lexical/symbol/locator token overlap; support: bounded non-graph channel overlap/rank points)
primary_relevance_signals: frozen plan source/scope match as a bounded eligibility filter (E)
supporting_signals: non-graph channel overlap/rank as bounded tie-break points (B/C/D)
structural provenance distance as final tie-break (G)
rejected_signals: non-graph support as a hard requirement (circularity — destroys bridge value)
selected_selectivity_design.score_transparency: a small number of interpretable signals with deterministic weights frozen at implementation-preregistration time in A5; reconstructible from recorded inputs; no opaque composite rules
selected_selectivity_design.deterministic_tie_break: selectivity score -> structural/provenance secondary key (path cost, then receipt order frozen at A5) -> stable object_id lexicographic; never database row order
selected_selectivity_design.no_hand_written_file_pattern_boosts: no special score bonuses for .C / README / macro/ / pgenerators/ or any positive-case-specific filename semantics; locator/title tokens are treated by one generic tokenizer for all candidates

selectivity_cap_design.rationale: generic absolute bound: at most 40% of the existing 20-slot bridge cap, keeping the bridge's additive graph footprint strictly below today's worst case while allowing multi-origin coverage; chosen from budget-architecture classes, not from case outcomes or case-specific candidate positions

no single provenance origin may consume the selectivity budget; this is the generic guard for the high-fan-out governed-provenance class that g020 exposed (one origin contributed all 112 fanned-out objects); the value is a generic bound on per-origin contribution, not derived from g020's exact 112->20 outcome
diversity_principles: preserve reasonable diversity across provenance origins, source files, and relations/workflow steps where multiple governed origins exist
never force artificial diversity when only one valid origin exists (a single-origin fan-out is simply bounded by PER_ORIGIN_CAP)
selectivity_cap_design.fail_closed: if no bridge candidate meets the generic relevance/selectivity criteria, admit none; reserved slots are never filled merely because budget exists
selectivity_cap_design.cap_semantics: SELECTIVITY_CAP and PER_ORIGIN_CAP are ceilings, not quotas: up to 8 candidates, never always 8

A_fixed_small_absolute_reservation.analysis: easy to audit, easy to replay, causally clean, bounded; strong default per the simplicity principle

B_small_fraction_of_rerank_pool.analysis: equivalent to A for a fixed pool but introduces a ratio parameter; no architectural benefit over a fixed absolute ceiling

C_dynamic_reservation_based_on_selected_.analysis: dynamic complexity without clear justification; harder to audit and replay; rejected unless a future stage demonstrates need

selected_admission_policy.family: A — fixed small absolute rerank-pool admission reservation
selected_admission_policy.displacement_semantics: retain the baseline fused top-N ordering, then replace the lowest-ranked eligible baseline entries with selected bridge candidates not already present, up to the admission budget; displaced object_ids are recorded
selected_admission_policy.no_duplicate_admission: a selected bridge candidate already present in the baseline rerank pool does not consume a reserved slot; deduplication by stable object identity; overlap recorded separately
selected_admission_policy.ceiling_not_quota: up to K candidates, never always K; empty reservation is a valid outcome (fail closed)
selected_admission_policy.candidate_authority: every specially admitted candidate remains GOVERNED_PROVENANCE_BACKED_ADDITIVE_RETRIEVAL_CANDIDATE with IDENTITY_AUTHORITY = NONE
selected_admission_policy.admission_grants: permission to compete in the reranker only — never answer authority, never final-selection priority; selection chances improve only through normal reranker/selector evaluation
selected_admission_policy.budget_rationale: generic class: small absolute reservation relative to the 30-slot rerank pool (2/30 ~ 7%, 3/30 = 10%), both preserving >= 90% ordinary-candidate competition; values chosen from budget-architecture classes, never from g036/g021 fused ranks (61/53) or any case-derived slot count
selected_admission_policy.budget_comparison_rule: A6 preregisters both budget arms ex ante against the same frozen baseline pool with preregistered decision criteria (bridge admission ratio, displacement accounting, control safety); the comparison is decided by those preregistered criteria, never by whether a positive case passes

selectivity_vs_admission_identifiability.SELECTIVITY_CAP: how many governed bridge candidates survive preselection into the graph stream
selectivity_vs_admission_identifiability.RERANK_ADMISSION_BUDGET: how many non-baseline bridge candidates may receive reserved rerank slots
selectivity_vs_admission_identifiability.staged_rationale: A3 froze CONTINUE_ONLY_AFTER_SELECTIVITY_DESIGN; an admission-only arm is not scientifically safe before selectivity is proven (g020 fan-out would let unselected provenance chunks monopolize reserved slots), so the factorial design's required proof (admission-only is safe enough to run) fails and S2 is invalid; S1 preserves clean attribution and minimizes treatment complexity

stage_1.stage: D3.5-A5 — Selectivity Prototype & Frozen-Trace Fan-Out Validation
stage_1.question: Can a generic deterministic selectivity policy materially reduce governed bridge fan-out and ordinary-candidate displacement while preserving the bridge candidates that are plausibly query-relevant?
stage_1.question_is_NOT: does final evidence recovery improve? (not asked in A5)

stage_2.stage: D3.5-A6 — Bounded Rerank-Admission Prototype & Paired Replay Validation
stage_2.question: With selectivity frozen, does bounded rerank-pool admission of selected bridge candidates improve downstream evidence competition without material control regression, under symmetric reranker-variance accounting?
stage_2.sequencing: only after A5 stabilizes selectivity and the replay fixture passes its verification gates

implementation_sequence: build compact tracked replay fixture from frozen A2 trace (mechanical, outcome-independent)
then A6 admission prototype with paired replay

selectivity_stage_outcome_surface.expected_evidence_boundary: expected evidence may only be used after candidate production for evaluation, never as a runtime input

future_experiment_design.anti_tuning_boundary: the selectivity policy and all parameters must be chosen from generic criteria before evaluating frozen case outcomes; tuning against retain ana_dpm.C / retain prod_sim_hvmaps.C / remove g020 candidates is prohibited and preregistered as a boundary here
future_experiment_design.exposed_cases_acknowledgment: reusing the frozen A2 six-case set is POST_OUTCOME_DESIGN_VALIDATION: these outcomes are already exposed, so the experiment is mechanistic development, not an unbiased confirmatory evaluation, and must never be represented as a fresh holdout
future_experiment_design.future_confirmation_boundary: any later claim of general validated improvement requires a separate untouched evaluation surface after the development redesign stabilizes; that evaluation is not scheduled now — the boundary is preserved only
future_experiment_design.runtime_selectivity_inspection_prohibiti: runtime selectivity cannot inspect case IDs, case roles, positive/control markers, or mechanism labels (g036/g021/g020/positive/control/Mechanism A/Mechanism C are evaluator-only)

before_any_replay_outcome: baseline top-30 rerank pool reproduced exactly
candidate payload reconstruction exact (semantic field equality: object_id, title, source_id, text payload, order; byte equality preferred, semantic equality required if serialization differs)
fixture_verification_gates.on_failure: STOP; do not run treatment evaluation on a non-equivalent fixture
fixture_verification_gates.reranker_input_equality_gate: baseline replay reranker inputs must match the original A2 baseline ordering/payload semantics before any treatment is introduced; approximate payload reconstruction is not accepted

control_failure_definition.CONTROL_MATERIAL_REGRESSION: loss of previously useful final evidence attributable to structured selectivity/admission displacement
control_failure_definition.numeric_threshold: none defined now; never derived from observed case outcomes

expansion_signal_definition.CONTROL_EXPANSION_SIGNAL: bridge/selectivity/admission consumes a disproportionate candidate budget (graph slots, selectivity cap, reserved slots) even without final metric regression
expansion_signal_definition.role: non-outcome diagnostic; recorded per case; does not automatically classify displacement as failure

exact_next_stage: D3.5-A5 — Selectivity Prototype & Frozen-Trace Fan-Out Validation

A5_scope.measure: fan-out/displacement/relevance retention with the frozen no-reranker metric surface

prohibited_actions: implement selectivity or admission inside A4
change bridge cap, graph weight, graph limit, or rerank pool size
run reranker replay or rerun A2
derive any budget from case-specific candidate positions
let the runtime selectivity policy inspect case IDs, roles, or mechanism labels
use expected evidence as a runtime input
